chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, who said:

I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'I intend to go out to some of the mountains.' He said, 'The people will inevitably face turbulence in their year.' I said to him, 'May I be your ransom! When we sell to them with credit (nasi'ah), it yields more profit.' He said, 'So sell them with a delay of one year.' I said, 'With a delay of two years?' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'With a delay of three?' He said, 'No.'
ai.seo_question: What is the maximum time limit for selling goods on credit according to Imam Al-Reza (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the jurisprudential boundaries of bay' al-nasi'ah (credit sale), establishing a maximum permissible credit term of two years to prevent excessive debt burden during periods of economic instability. The Imam’s rejection of a three-year delay highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on balancing commercial profit with social justice, ensuring that credit extension does not lead to unsustainable financial entanglement for the buyer.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad who said,

‘I said to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What is inevitable for the people is that they are shaken in this year of theirs (financially turbulent times)’. So I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! When we sell to them by credit it is more profitable’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So sell them with a delay for a year’. I said, ‘(What about) with a delay for two years?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes’. I said, ‘With a delay for three?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from who has said the following:

“I once said to abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘I like to travel to certain areas of the mountains.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘This year people will not be able to avoid difficult times.’ I then said, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, if we sell to them goods on credit with deferred payment it is more profitable. He (the Imam) said, ‘Sell to them for one year deferred payment.’ I asked, ‘Can we defer payment for two years?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, you can do so.’ I then asked, ‘Can we defer payment for three years?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘No, you cannot do so.’”
